body:
## Problem

- A member connects an MCP server from Desktop, the toast says it was added, the tag says "Connected" — and the server lists no tools. Nothing anywhere says why.
- `discoverGatewayTools` runs right after a connect. Both call sites drop its outcome: the connect path has `onError: () => {}`, the register path has `.catch(() => null)`. A listing that fails, and a registry row that has gone missing, both land as silence.
- The moment the listing fails is the one moment the app knows the server cannot be used. That is the moment this PR makes it say so.

Origin: [Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09G8Q32R6F/p1789729160124739).

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0b560-9d38-7bc4-9670-f8b13e846b6a -->
## Origin

- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-09-18
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0b560-9d38-7bc4-9670-f8b13e846b6a)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0b560-9d38-7bc4-9670-f8b13e846b6a -->

## Changes

- Both discovery paths warn when the listing fails, so a server that answered nothing no longer sits at "Connected" with an empty tool list.
- A registry row that has vanished (`no-server`) reports the same way — the user is left with the same empty server either way.
- A credential that is mid-OAuth (`no-connection`) still passes quietly. The server's own tag already says "Finishing setup", and a toast would only repeat it.
- The toast is a fixed recovery message, never the upstream reason. That reason is the refresh endpoint's `detail`, which can carry a fragment of the upstream server's response body.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This makes the failure legible. It does not fix the 502 behind the report, which is a deployment setting — see below.

<details>
<summary>What the 502 actually is, and why no code here fixes it</summary>

The proxy endpoint answers 502 for every call in any deployment that routes egress through an `HTTP(S)_PROXY`:

- `PinnedTransport` refuses a proxied request unless `SSRF_TRUSTED_PROXY_URLS` names that proxy. The setting arrived with the pinned client in #102376 and defaults to empty, so nothing is declared and the gate closes on everything.
- The MCP store is the only caller of `pinned_client`, so it takes the whole failure. OAuth, DCR and the catalog probe run on `requests`, which has no such gate — which is why a connection authenticates and then cannot fetch a single tool.

| Path | Client | Proxy gate | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MCP proxy, tool sync, tool call | `pinned_client` (httpx) | fail closed | 502 on every call |
| OAuth, DCR, discovery, probe | `requests` | none | healthy |

**The fix is to name the egress proxy in `SSRF_TRUSTED_PROXY_URLS`**, in deployment config rather than in this repo.

An earlier revision of this PR made an empty allowlist fall back to using the environment proxy. That is reverted. Review pointed out — correctly, and it is verifiable in `PinnedTransport.handle_request` — that the proxy branch never rewrites the request to the validated address, so the fallback silently disabled DNS-rebinding protection on URLs a user supplies. Trading that away to restore a route is a call for whoever owns the deployment, not a default this client should pick.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

- `still registers the server when the tool listing fails, and says so` catches the handler going silent again, and pins the message to the fixed recovery text rather than the upstream reason.
- `reports a server that vanished from the registry before the listing` catches the `no-server` skip, which resolved successfully and so bypassed the error handler entirely.
- Not checked: no rendering of the toast. The handlers are covered by the tests above.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5

Started from the inbox report's own next step — the outbound allowlist for `mcp.stripe.com`. Reproducing the endpoint through `pinned_client` with no proxy in the environment succeeded, which moved the search to the proxy branch of the transport and then to the setting that gates it. #102376 landed the day before the report.

That diagnosis was first shipped here as a code change, making an unset allowlist fall back to the environment proxy. It is reverted for the reason in the collapsed section. What remains is the half that stands on its own and weakens nothing.

Duplicate search: `gh pr list --state open --search "mcp_store proxy"`. #102930 comes from this same report and carries the web-side visibility — the persisted sync error and the status tag — and notes that Desktop parity needs its own change. This is part of that, and touches no file it touches. #99739 changes the proxy's exception mapping and is untouched here.

Review taken: CodeRabbit raised CWE-209 on rendering `Error.message` in the toast (fixed message now), and the missing `no-server` / `no-connection` cases (`no-server` handled, `no-connection` deliberately not, for the reason in Changes). parameterai raised the SSRF regression that led to the revert. The CodeRabbit CLI is not installed in this sandbox, so the only passes are the reviews posted on the PR.
